title: Stranger Things
synopsis: Hawkins. One more rift. The party is older, the stakes are bigger, and the math homework is, somehow, still due Monday.

nodes.text: The pool drains weirdly. The lifeguard, who is also Steve, notices first. Robin, beside him, is already calling Dustin. Eleven, On the Phone will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Call the whole party in” than after “Investigate quietly first.”

choices.consequence: You commit to call the whole party in. It carries you toward Eleven, On the Phone, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You commit to investigate quietly first. It carries you toward Eleven, On the Phone, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: El is two states away at school. The call drops twice. The third time she just says, 'I'm coming.' She is. The Wheeler Basement is already waiting. What changes is whether “Wait for her” or “Start without her” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You choose to wait for her. By The Wheeler Basement, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You start without her. The path to The Wheeler Basement opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: The party reassembles around a kitchen table that has, somehow, more spreadsheets than the FBI. The New Kid is already waiting. What changes is whether “Plan first” or “Move first” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You commit to plan first. It carries you toward The New Kid, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You move first. The path to The New Kid opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: A transfer student named Vera knows more about the Upside Down than she should. She also runs cross-country. Hopper's House is already waiting. What changes is whether “Recruit Vera” or “Watch Vera carefully” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You recruit Vera. The path to Hopper's House opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You choose to watch Vera carefully. By Hopper's House, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Hopper has a cabin, a beer, and a tired face. He wants to help. He also wants you to be careful. Max, Recovering comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Ask for the gun” and “Ask for his old files.”

choices.consequence: You choose to ask for the gun. By Max, Recovering, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to ask for his old files. By Max, Recovering, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: Max walks now. She is, against her own will, the quietest of the group. She has, you realize, opinions about the rift you have not yet asked for. Will's Headache comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Make her tactical lead” and “Let her opt in.”

choices.consequence: You commit to make her tactical lead. It carries you toward Will's Headache, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You commit to let her opt in. It carries you toward Will's Headache, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Will starts feeling it again. He hates feeling it again. He does not, however, hide. The road still runs toward The Library Microfiche. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Use Will's connection” and choosing “Protect Will first.”

choices.consequence: You commit to use Will's connection. It carries you toward The Library Microfiche, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.
You choose to protect Will first. By The Library Microfiche, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.consequence: You photograph the article. The path to Vera's Confession opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
You commit to find the old witnesses. It carries you toward Vera's Confession, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Vera admits she's been tracking the rifts since her family lost a brother in 1989. She is, you realize, also a survivor. Both choices lead to Tunnels Under Town, but “Make her co-lead” arrives there with a different cost than “Make sure she's okay first.”

choices.consequence: You commit to make her co-lead. It carries you toward Tunnels Under Town, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: There are tunnels. There are always tunnels. The town's pipes have been a map for years and nobody noticed. The road still runs toward Steve and Robin's Bicker. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Map the tunnels” and choosing “Go in tonight.”

choices.consequence: You choose to map the tunnels. By Steve and Robin's Bicker, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: They bicker. They are best friends. They are working. The team is, in their own way, held together by them. The Demogorgon's Cousin is already waiting. What changes is whether “Send them as a pair” or “Send them separately” is the instinct you carry into it.

nodes.text: A new monster — smaller, faster, somehow politer about doors. You hate that you noticed the politeness. The road still runs toward Lab Records. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Engage cautiously” and choosing “Hit it hard.”

choices.consequence: You commit to engage cautiously. It carries you toward Lab Records, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Hopper's old files contain the names of researchers still alive. One is, you discover, in Indianapolis. He will, on the phone, say one sentence and hang up. The road still runs toward Eleven Arrives. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Drive to Indianapolis” and choosing “Send Steve in your stead.”

choices.consequence: You choose to drive to Indianapolis. By Eleven Arrives, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You send Steve in your stead. The path to Eleven Arrives opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: El, in the rain, in a denim jacket. The room exhales. You realize you have, despite the spreadsheets, been waiting for her exactly this long. Both choices lead to The First Skirmish, but “Lead with her” arrives there with a different cost than “Center the team, with her.”

choices.consequence: You lead with her. The path to The First Skirmish opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: A skirmish at the pool. Nobody dies. Two get hurt. The monster retreats. You understand its pattern. The road still runs toward The Indianapolis Researcher. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Press the advantage” and choosing “Plan the second.”

choices.consequence: You choose to press the advantage. By The Indianapolis Researcher, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You commit to plan the second. It carries you toward The Indianapolis Researcher, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: He says, in his apartment, 'You'll have to close it from inside.' He is, you can tell, telling you the truth he has been afraid to tell for thirty years. Max's Plan will follow either decision, but it will meet a different version of you after “Accept the cost” than after “Look for another way.”

choices.consequence: You accept the cost. The path to Max's Plan opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: Max draws, on a napkin, a plan that involves all of you, no martyr. The plan is, you suspect, the one El has been quietly thinking too. The Mall, Empty comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Approve Max's plan” and “Refine it with the group.”

choices.consequence: You choose to approve Max's plan. By The Mall, Empty, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.
You choose to refine it with the group. By The Mall, Empty, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

nodes.text: The mall, again. It is, somehow, always the mall. The rift glows above the food court. You realize you have grown up in this building. The road still runs toward Vera's Choice. Its next turn depends on the difference between choosing “Step in” and choosing “Anchor outside.”

choices.consequence: You commit to step in. It carries you toward Vera's Choice, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: Vera offers to be the inside-person. So does Will. So, in his way, does Steve. You decide who. The Close is already waiting. What changes is whether “Send Vera” or “Send Will” is the instinct you carry into it.

choices.consequence: You commit to send Vera. It carries you toward The Close, exchanging a familiar uncertainty for a consequence nobody has modeled.

nodes.text: The rift, with the team's coordinated push, closes for the last time. The fluorescents flicker. The town does not, this time, lose a kid. The Parking Lot comes either way; its meaning changes with the difference between “Stand in the empty mall together” and “Walk out into the parking lot.”

choices.text: Stand in the empty mall together
choices.consequence: You stand in the empty mall together. The path to The Parking Lot opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

choices.text: Walk out into the parking lot

nodes.text: Cars, summer, the team. You realize you will all, eventually, leave this town. Tonight, though, you are right where you should be. To choose “Throw a party at the Wheelers'” means meeting Party Together; “Just go to Steve's job for ice cream” sends you toward Hawkins, After instead. A third choice, “Take the third path,” keeps Out Into the World in play.

choices.text: Throw a party at the Wheelers'
choices.consequence: You choose to throw a party at the Wheelers'. By Party Together, the decision has become data, precedent, and a problem larger than the person who made it.

choices.text: Just go to Steve's job for ice cream
choices.consequence: You just go to Steve's job for ice cream. The path to Hawkins, After opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.
Some endings reveal themselves last. You take the third path. The path to Out Into the World opens, and the system registers the move before anyone admits the rules have changed.

nodes.text: You stay close — through college, through breakups, through one wedding and one funeral. The party never breaks up. You realize, late, that the rift was never the point. The friendships were. The road into Party Together began with “Throw a party at the Wheelers'” in The Parking Lot; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You stay in Hawkins. You become a person who watches the town for next time. Next time, mercifully, does not come. The road into Hawkins, After began with “Just go to Steve's job for ice cream” in The Parking Lot; here, that decision stops being a moment and becomes a life.

You leave Hawkins and never quite leave it. Wherever you go, a part of you is in that basement around that table. You take the lesson — that a small group of kids can save a town — into every other room of your life.
